issues.title: `react/no-danger` set to "warn" provides no CI enforcement
issues.description: The `lint` script is bare `eslint` with no `--max-warnings=0`, so a warning-level rule exits 0 and the CI Lint step passes; a future PR introducing `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sails through with only a log line nobody reads. This directly contradicts the block's own comment that these rules are "guardrails that fail loudly" — it should be `"error"` like the other two rules (or the lint script should add `--max-warnings=0`).

issues.title: `trust: true` selector is easily bypassed and the comment overstates its coverage
issues.description: `Property[key.name='trust'][value.value=true]` only matches identifier keys with a literal `true`, so `{ "trust": true }` (string-quoted key has no `key.name`), shorthand `{ trust }`, computed keys, and `trust: someFlag` all slip past, while the adjacent comment claims the rule is "Broad enough to catch `{ trust: true }` elsewhere too". Add a second selector for literal keys (`Property[key.value='trust'][value.value=true]`) or document the gaps so the rule is treated as a best-effort tripwire rather than a guarantee.

issues.title: rehype-raw ban misses dynamic imports and subpath imports
issues.description: `no-restricted-imports` with `paths` only flags static imports of exactly `"rehype-raw"`; `await import("rehype-raw")` and subpath imports like `"rehype-raw/lib/index.js"` are not reported. Using `patterns: ["rehype-raw", "rehype-raw/*"]` and noting the dynamic-import blind spot would make the guardrail match its stated intent (low impact today since the package isn't installed, so any import fails the build anyway).
